newsitem.title: UK: EMAP says majority of board backs chairman.
newsitem.headline: EMAP says majority of board backs chairman.

text.p: EMAP Plc, the UK media to exhibitions group, said on Thursday its board had given majority backing to its chairman Sir John Hoskyns, with the exception of two non-executive directors.

Hoskyns position had come under review following a call from one of the non-executive directors Ken Simmonds for the chairman to be removed. EMAP said it would hold an extraordinary general meeting in the near future to recommend the removal of Simmonds and Joe Cooke from the board.

EMAP shares had been weighed down this session by a press report of disagreements among top management, including the chief executive, fuelling speculation that one of the group's chiefs would have to go.
Shares were down 32 pence at 712 1/2 by the close of Thursday's trading.
A report in Thursday's Financial Times newspaper revived concerns about management discord, claiming that the board was "riven by dispute" and had been for years.
It also said that relations between chief executive Robin Miller and managing director David Arculus were "strained."
The chairman's position came under pressure due to a rift over new procedures for removing directors, according to a Financial Times report earlier this week.
Some directors were reported to be concerned that the rule changes would make it easier to force out "difficult directors."
The changes mean directors can be removed with the support of 75 percent of the board.
